title: Share, embed, SCIM and OAuth token swaps never mutate a session-backed SecurityContext, and SessionService.runAs restores the prior context object — a guest request can no longer rewrite the session's identity or keep a revoked token alive on the cookie alone

criteria.given: ShareTokenAuthFilter and EmbedAuthFilter (view, authoring and public-grant paths all funnel through the same swap)
criteria.then: they build a fresh context (SecurityContextHolder.createEmptyContext) and install it with setContext, and never call SecurityContextHolder.getContext().setAuthentication(...) — with a logged-in session cookie that returns the object stored in the HttpSession, so the old pattern rewrote the session's identity

criteria.given: the OAuthBearerAuthenticationFilter and the ScimAuthFilter, which mint request-scoped identities with the same pattern
criteria.then: they swap a fresh context object the same way, so a bearer token on a request that carries a logged-in cookie cannot rewrite that session either

it installs the owner identity in a fresh context object and restores the prior context object in finally, so while a guest request runs under the owner's scope the session-stored context (and any concurrent cookie-only request) never sees the owner's identity

each of the four filters and SessionService.runAs is covered by a test that installs a session-backed SecurityContext (the object a logged-in cookie would have in the HttpSession) and asserts the object, its principal and its authorities are unchanged during and after the swap — nothing guest- or owner-shaped persists, so a revoked token stops working on the cookie alone
